01-top-playtime.webp: Horizontal bars show the top 20 games by hours played. Halo: The Master Chief Collection leads, followed by Hell Let Loose and Phasmophobia. The remaining displayed order is Rocksmith 2014 Edition REMASTERED LEARN & PLAY; Call of Duty; Destiny 2; Halo Infinite; Fallout 4; Dying Light 2 Stay Human: Reloaded Edition; 7 Days to Die; Barotrauma; PAYDAY 2; Resident Evil 5; Dying Light; Metro Exodus; Resident Evil 6; Stardew Valley; State of Decay 2: Juggernaut Edition; Satisfactory; Call of Duty: World at War. The leading bar reaches about 900 hours; the shortest displayed bars are around 100 hours.
02-playtime-distribution.webp: Histogram of games by hours played. The first bin near zero is overwhelmingly the tallest, above 120 games. Counts drop sharply in the following bins. A sparse tail extends to roughly 900 hours. Most games have little playtime while a few receive much more.
03-steam-deck-status.webp: Horizontal bars count games by Steam Deck compatibility. Categories descend in size: playable, verified, unsupported, unknown. Playable is clearly largest; verified is next; unknown is smallest. The count axis extends beyond 160 games. This is a bar chart.
04-release-years.webp: The line shows game counts by release year, approximately 2006 to 2026. Counts generally rise toward the mid-to-late 2010s. The largest peak is at 2018, above 35 games. Counts then fall sharply into the early 2020s, fluctuate, and end near zero in 2026. Release year is not purchase year or the year a game was played.
05-metascore-distribution.webp: Histogram of games by Metascore, spanning roughly the high 40s to the mid-90s. Most games cluster between about 75 and 90, with the tallest bins around the low 80s. Low scores are uncommon. The vertical axis counts games.
06-top-metascore.webp: Horizontal bars show 20 games with similar high Metascores in the low-to-mid 90s. Displayed order: Half-Life; Half-Life 2; BioShock; Baldur's Gate 3; Portal 2; The Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim; BioShock Infinite; The Elder Scrolls IV: Oblivion Game of the Year Edition (2009); Red Dead Redemption 2; Beat Saber; The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt; Call of Duty 4: Modern Warfare (2007); Okami HD; Tom Clancy's Splinter Cell Chaos Theory; Call of Duty (2003); Dragon Age: Origins - Ultimate Edition; METAL GEAR SOLID V: THE PHANTOM PAIN; Resident Evil 4; Batman: Arkham City - Game of the Year Edition; Fallout 3: Game of the Year Edition. Several bars have equal visible lengths, so display order does not establish a strict ranking within ties.
07-userscore-vs-metascore.webp: Scatter plot comparing Metascore horizontally with user score vertically. Most points cluster around Metascores of 75 to 95 and user scores of 80 to 100. There is a broad upward association, considerable variation, and lower user-score outliers even among games with strong Metascores. Points have no game labels.
08-top-tags.webp: Horizontal bars count the top 20 tags. Displayed descending order: single-player; singleplayer; family sharing; spanish - spain; steam achievements; action; controller support any; multiplayer any; adventure; multiplayer; steam cloud; atmospheric; steam trading cards; simplified chinese; full controller support; co-op any; portuguese - brazil; first-person; shooter; traditional chinese. Single-player is highest; the next two bars are visually equal. Although the chart title says non-language, language labels are included in the saved image.
09-platform-support.webp: Horizontal bars show declared platform support counts. Windows is supported by far more games than macOS or Linux. macOS is second and Linux third, with those two much closer to each other than to Windows. The count axis extends beyond 300 games. These are declared support counts, rather than verified compatibility tests.
10-modes.webp: Horizontal bars count Single-player, Co-op and Multi-player tags. Single-player dominates, extending beyond 300 games. Co-op and Multi-player have very small bars close to zero in this saved image. This is a tag-based snapshot; other tag charts on this page include frequent multiplayer and co-op labels, so these counts should not be treated as a complete inventory of game capabilities.
11-hours-by-deck.webp: Box plots compare hours-played distributions for playable, verified, unsupported and unknown Steam Deck categories. Unsupported has the highest visible median, followed by verified, playable and unknown. Verified has the widest visible spread and highest upper whisker; unsupported is next; playable is narrower. Unknown is concentrated close to zero. These are playtime distributions, rather than total hours summed per category.
12-hours-vs-metascore.webp: Scatter plot of Metascore against hours played. The hours axis is logarithmic, with ticks from 0.01 to 1,000 hours; equal vertical steps represent multiplication rather than equal numbers of hours. Games scoring around 75 to 95 span tiny fractions of an hour to hundreds of hours. Higher scores do not show a simple steady increase in playtime. Points have no game labels.
13-top-tags-heavy.webp: Horizontal bars count the top 20 tags among games played for more than 20 hours. Displayed order: spanish - spain; single-player; singleplayer; action; family sharing; multiplayer any; multiplayer; steam achievements; controller support any; co-op any; first-person; steam cloud; co-op.1; simplified chinese; shooter; traditional chinese; atmospheric; fps; adventure; portuguese - brazil. Several lower bars have equal visible lengths. Language and feature tags are present alongside genre tags; co-op.1 is the label printed in the saved image.
14-metascore-buckets.webp: Bars count games in Metascore intervals [0, 50), [50, 60), [60, 70), [70, 80), [80, 90), and [90, 100). The [80, 90) group is largest, nearly reaching 100 games. [70, 80) is second, [90, 100) third, then [60, 70). Groups below 60 have very few games. Each written interval includes its lower bound and excludes its upper bound.
15-total-hours-by-year.webp: The line groups total hours played by game release year, approximately 2010 to 2025. The largest peak is at 2019, above 1,400 hours. Another high point appears at 2021, above 1,000 hours. Totals decline through 2023, rise in 2024, then drop sharply in 2025. Earlier years are lower and variable, with a pronounced low in 2014. This groups lifetime playtime by release year; it does not show hours played during each calendar year.
